definitions.explanation: An involuntary shaking of the body or a part of the body, caused by cold, fear, excitement, illness, or other strong physical or emotional states.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}さで{体|からだ}に{震|ふる}えが{来|き}た。
examples.english: My body started shivering from the cold.

examples.japanese: {恐怖|きょうふ}で{声|こえ}に{震|ふる}えが{混|ま}じっていた。
examples.english: There was a tremor in her voice from fear.

notes: The noun form of the verb {震|ふる}える (to tremble/shake). Common collocations include {震|ふる}えが{止|と}まらない (can't stop shaking), {震|ふる}えが{来|く}る (start trembling), and {声|こえ}の{震|ふる}え (tremor in the voice). Can also be written as {振|ふる}え, though {震|ふる}え is more common for involuntary shaking. {手|て}の{震|ふる}え (hand tremor) is frequently discussed in medical contexts.
